title: Curves in the sense of file 06
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]. Then $X$ is a smooth *connected curve over $k$* in the sense of [def-sc-curves]: $X$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], its underlying topological space has Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

proof.text: Unfolding the hypothesis. By [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], $X$ is a curve over $k$ in the sense of [def-pc-curve] whose structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is smooth and projective. By [def-pc-curve], $X$ is a variety over $k$ of dimension $1$: the scheme $X$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], its structure morphism is separated and of finite type, and $\dim X=1$ in the sense of [def-pc-dimension], i.e. $\sup_{x\in X}\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=1$ (the supremum of the Krull dimensions of the local rings of $X$). Projectivity is not used below.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: 'By [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] $X$ is a curve over $k$, hence a variety: integral, with $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ separated and of finite type ([def-pc-curve])'

proof.text: $X$ is nonempty and irreducible. An integral scheme is nonempty by the definition [def-pc-integral-scheme], and its underlying topological space is irreducible by [lem-pc-integral-scheme-irreducible] (Stacks 01ON), applied to the integral scheme $X$ of step 1.

source.place: Properties, Lemma Tag 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral); blueprint proof: 'in particular $X$ is nonempty'

proof.text: $X$ is connected. The underlying topological space of $X$ is irreducible (step 2), hence connected by [lem-pc-irreducible-space-connected]; so the scheme $X$ is connected in the sense of [def-weil-connected-scheme] (which includes nonemptiness).

source.place: Topology, sentence after Definition Tag 004V: 'An irreducible space is obviously connected'; blueprint proof: 'connected (being irreducible)'

proof.text: $X$ has dimension one in the sense of [def-sc-curves]. The dimension of a scheme in [def-sc-curves] is the Krull dimension of its underlying topological space [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (Stacks, Properties, Definition Tag 04MT). By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] (Stacks 04MU), this Krull dimension equals $\sup_{x\in X}\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$, which is $1$ by step 1. Hence the underlying space of $X$ has Krull dimension $1$, in particular at most $1$.

source.place: Properties, Definition Tag 04MT and Lemma Tag 04MU (lemma-dimension), (1)=(2); blueprint proof: 'being a curve, of dimension $1$'

proof.text: Conclusion. The field $k$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], as [def-sc-curves] requires. By step 1, $X$ is separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and by step 4 its dimension is at most one; so $X$ is a curve over $k$ in the sense of [def-sc-curves]. It is nonempty and connected (steps 2 and 3) and of dimension one (step 4), so it is a connected curve; and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] by step 1, so it is smooth in the sense of [def-sc-curves]. This proves the claim.

source.place: ## Proof, last sentences: 'Its structure morphism is smooth by hypothesis, and [def-sc-curves] requires exactly: nonempty, connected, separated scheme of finite type of dimension one, smooth over $k$.'
